text: @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr 将 witr_trace 接入 DSH 工具系统，调用本机 witr 追踪进程、端口或文件目标，并返回进程来源诊断。目标可用进程号、端口、进程名或文件路径指定；输出支持标准文本、树形、Mermaid、DOT 和 JSON，也可对进程名启用精确匹配。未指定类型的数字会先按进程号查询，未找到时再尝试端口。适用于开发或运维时定位端口占用者、进程父级和文件锁持有者。使用前需安装 witr，可从 PATH 查找或设置 binaryPath，并可调整超时。

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr adds witr_trace to DSH to trace processes, ports, and files through the local witr executable. It supports text, tree, Mermaid, DOT, and JSON results, helping identify process ancestry, port owners, and file-lock holders. Install witr first.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · `dsh-plugin-witr`：**The causal process & port tracing plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).** [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [](https://github.com/martinm86867-ops/witr) [](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)

Gives autonomous DeepSeek agents instant root-cause visibility into running processes, port collisions (EADDRINUSE), and stuck file locks.

---

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · The Problem：Autonomous agents frequently stall during development or operational loops when encountering state conflicts:
- A local dev server fails to start with `EADDRINUSE: 3080`.
- An environment command hangs because `/var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend` is locked.
- A long-lived background worker holds memory, but `ps aux` only shows an uninformative child process without context.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · The Problem：Standard agent workarounds—chaining `ps aux`, `lsof`, `fuser`, `netstat`, and `kill -9`—are fragile, hallucination-prone, and risk accidentally terminating the parent terminal or shell.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · The Solution：`dsh-plugin-witr` wires [`witr`](https://github.com/martinm86867-ops/witr) directly into the DeepSeek Harness tool registry via the **Cordis** plugin lifecycle.

Instead of guessing, the agent calls `witr_trace` to receive the complete supervisor hierarchy from `systemd` down through terminal emulators, shells, and parent containers in a single deterministic turn.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · Features：- **Full Causal Ancestry:** Traces processes backwards through `systemd -> ptyxis -> bash -> node -> esbuild` to pinpoint what launched and maintains the target.
- **Port Collision Resolution:** Translates port numbers (e.g. `3080`, `8080`) directly into the owning PID, parent shell, working directory, and active Git branch.
- **File Lock Diagnostics:** Pinpoints which background process or daemon holds open a file descriptor.
- **Multi-Format Projection:** Supports human-readable diagnostic text, compact hierarchical trees, JSON, and **Mermaid.js flowchart diagrams** for visual documentation. JSON output omits process environment variables, so tracing a process never copies its secrets into the model context.
- **DeepSeek Plugin Manager UI:** Fully declared Cordis bundle with localized metadata, an icon, and configurable runtime parameters in the Web UI.
- **Exit-Code Fidelity:** Classifies every trace from `witr`'s documented exit codes instead of scraping its output, so warnings, "not found", and "insufficient privileges" arrive as answers and only genuinely broken runs fail the call.
- **Cancellation & Safety:** Strictly

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · Model Tool Specification: `witr_trace`：`kind`, `format`, and `target` are validated before `witr` runs, so an out-of-vocabulary
`kind` or `format` is rejected instead of silently ignored.

**Target inference.** With no `kind`, a bare number is tried as a process ID first and then as a
port, a value containing `/` is treated as a file path, and anything else is a process name. Non-empty
targets are passed to `witr` after a `--` terminator, so a process name that begins with `-` is never
misread as a command-line flag.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · Model Tool Specification: `witr_trace`：**Working directory.** A relative `file` target is resolved against the calling session's working
directory rather than the directory the harness process was launched from. When that directory is
unavailable for an agent call, a relative `file` target is refused instead of silently resolving
against the harness process directory — retry with an absolute path.

**Concurrency.** The tool is read-only, so it is marked concurrency-safe and several traces may share
one tool batch.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · Outcomes：The plugin reads [`witr`'s exit codes](https://github.com/pranshuparmar/witr#72-exit-codes) rather
than matching output text — witr documents the codes as the contract and the wording of its
human-readable output as explicitly outside it. Only the outcomes that carry no answer fail the tool
call:

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · Outcomes：| `witr` exit | Meaning | Tool result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | Found, clean | Answer |
| `1` | Found, with warnings | **Answer** — warnings are the diagnostic payload |
| `2` | Not found | Answer; also drives the PID → port fallback |
| `3` | Insufficient privileges | Answer — witr's own output says how to escalate |
| `4` | Invalid input, or an ambiguous name | Error; retry with `exact: true` or a fuller name |
| `5` | Internal error | Error |
| `6` | Found, but the cause can't be traced | **Answer** |
| — | `witr` could not be started at all | Error naming `binaryPath` |
| any other non-zero | Unrecognized status (signal, timeout, or a future `witr` code) | Error — never mistaken for an answer |

@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-witr README · Configuration Schema：Configured via Cordis YAML or the DeepSeek Web Settings UI:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `binaryPath` | `string` | `"witr"` | Path to the `witr` binary. Blank values fall back to `"witr"`. |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `10000` | Subprocess execution timeout in milliseconds (minimum `1`; unusable values fall back to `10000`). |
